questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses available to me at the host university and its academic reputation

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. The university website had a detailed checklist of things to do prior to and upon arrival. And the international office was helpful with answering questions I had regarding course registration.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an introductory meeting for echange students at the faculty of humanities by the international office.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was lucky and was offered housing through the UvA Student Housing. I would recommend applying for that even though they have limited availability. I was told towards the end of June that I would be offered housing. Otherwise I recommend starting early looking for housing as it can be hard to find.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I don't think it's possible to live on campus... Public transport is expensive, but it's easy to get around by bike (so similar to Copenhagen, except the bikes don't seem to be following any traffic rules.)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's obviously not luxury housing, but it wasn't bad.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The course registration is done through an online portal on a first come, first served principle. Different faculties and different courses have different registration periods and different portals, which is slightly confusing. The university sends an email with the information when the registration periods approach. The semester is divided in three blocks, and it's possible to change courses for the second and third block during the first block (if there are still free spots left.)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international office was very helpful in answering my questions both by phone and email. During the semester one of my professors helped me switch a course that was not available to me in the original registration process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I successfully registered to all the courses I wanted except one.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register to one or two extra courses as you might not get a spot on the ones you want or you might be waitlisted. If there are some courses in the second or third block that it seems like you are not able to take, then try asking a professor or student advisor for help once you're there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was a very high academic level. The workload is intense, but the academic outcome was very rewarding.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was a similar mix of lectures and student involved teaching, though more student presentations than I am used to. The preparation for class was a lot more work heavy as there were regular assignments and different kinds of running assessment that counted towards the final grade. I had approx. an assignment a week on top of the readings for class. There was also more group work than I am used to from UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Language in Use: Variation and Acquisition
How Literature Shapes Society
Sign Linguistics 1
Contact, Conflict and the Media
Term Paper Linguistics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I highly recommend Sign Linguistics 1. It was very interesting to see language and concepts about language from a different perspective. The professor and the other students were all curious about the subject which made for some good discussions. The workload was also less intense than the other courses I took.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I paid a monthly subscription of around 20 euro at swapfiets to rent a bike. I think it's possible to buy a used bike for cheaper, but with swapfiets you get a good bike that you can get repaired for free and don't have the hassle of reselling it afterwards.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transportation was expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university offers both athletic and creative activities at a discount, but I didn't participate in any. The Erasmus Student Network also organises events and gives a discount at a language school for Dutch lessons.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend participating in the ESN intro week to meet fellow exchange students. I also recommend the ESN discounted Dutch course although I didn't learn much Dutch. It was a nice way to meet people and to learn a little about Dutch culture.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend visiting some of the many, many museums. If you register at the municipality upon arrival and get a BSN number, you can get a museumkaart for 65 euro that gives free acces to most museums for a year. I especially enjoyed the canal museum (Grachtenmuseum) and the Tropenmuseum.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, it's quite similar to Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Nope, I met some Dutch students in my courses, but mostly socialized with other internationals. There are a lot of international students doing their full degrees in Amsterdam though.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The seeming lack of traffic rules for bikes could be both confusing and frustrating at times.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I liked the stroopwaffels. And how easy it was to get around in the city to explore new areas.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for an intense workload throughout the whole semester and not just at the end. That's the most important.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really...

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The academic gain and meeting new people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The groupwork for one of my courses, where I got unlucky with my group. And final assignments due on the 25th and 28th of December...

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
